draft.title: The skeletal system
card: Bones hold the body up and give it its shape. This is support. They also protect organs: the skull covers the brain and the ribs cover the heart and lungs.
Bones act as levers. A muscle pulls on a bone, and the bone turns around a joint to move part of the body.
moves in one line, like a door, bending and straightening. The elbow and knee are examples.
moves in many directions, including rotation. The shoulder and hip are examples.
draft.remember: Bones support, protect and act as levers, and each type of joint allows its own kind of movement.

a.q: Which joint lets the arm swing in a full circle at the shoulder?
opts: Ball-and-socket joint
Hinge joint
Lever joint
Support joint
a.why: The shoulder is a ball-and-socket joint, which moves in many directions and can rotate. A hinge joint only bends and straightens in one line, so it cannot swing the arm in a circle.
a.clue: Think about which joint moves in many directions.

b.q: Jin bends and straightens his knee as he kicks a football. Which statement best explains how this movement happens?
opts: Muscles pull on bones, which turn around a hinge joint
Muscles pull on bones, which turn on a ball-and-socket joint
Bones pull on muscles, which turn around a hinge joint
Bones move alone, because bones hold the body up
b.why: The knee is a hinge joint, and a muscle pulling on a bone makes the bone act as a lever around it. A ball-and-socket joint would allow rotation in many directions, which is not how the knee bends and straightens.
b.clue: Which joint moves in one line like a door?

b.best: Muscles pull on bones, which turn around a hinge joint

problems.detail: Too easy for Year 11. 'Lever joint' and 'Support joint' are not real joint types, so only 'Hinge joint' is a plausible distractor. The clue ('which joint moves in many directions') then points straight to the answer, so a student needs no real understanding to get it right.

a.q: Which movement can the hip make that the knee cannot?
opts: Swinging the leg around in a circle
Bending the leg at the joint
Straightening the leg at the joint
Moving the leg when a muscle pulls on a bone
a.why: The hip is a ball-and-socket joint, so it moves in many directions and can swing the leg in a circle. The knee is a hinge joint, so it can also bend and straighten, and muscles pull on bones at both joints.
